- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is falling sharply.
- Model frequently overshoots after a sharp price spike (e.g., +5–10% from prior day) — cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch the reversal — increase forecast slope gently toward sentiment direction.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model tends to continue falling; if sentiment turns positive, adjust forecast to reflect potential rebound.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period price (last 7–10 days) — increase forecast tail end by 0.5–1.5% relative to earlier days if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment is high and price is falling, model may misread sentiment — forecast should not drop below 1–2% below recent low unless sentiment confirms bearish shift.
